description:
Cargo.toml line 20-21:

  serde = ["dep:serde"]

In src/lib.rs the serde derives are applied only to IdentityError:

  #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
  pub enum IdentityError { ... }

The Cargo.toml comment says this is for caching/transport in pkix-chain::Error 'AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6'. But that same non-negotiable says:

> Public result/error types ... MUST derive Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Eq and MUST be Send + Sync. They SHOULD support serde::Serialize + Deserialize behind a `serde` feature flag for cross-process / persistent caches.

ServerName and MailboxName are 'public result types' the moment they appear in caller-side caches. Per the cross-process-cache use case explicitly called out in non-negotiable #6: a sidecar process that pre-validates identity-bindings and serializes the verdict needs to serialize BOTH the identity (ServerName/MailboxName, as the cache key) AND the verdict (Ok or IdentityError).

Today: the verdict can be serialized but the key cannot. Workaround: caller serializes the *input string* and replays parse on every cache hit. That's correct but defeats parse-once semantics.

Recommend: add Serialize/Deserialize derives to ServerName and MailboxName under the serde feature. This forces a Serialize-shape decision (internal representation: tagged union? Or wire as the canonical normalized string?) — file that as the design question.

This also forces resolution of PKIX-68mt.21 (lifetime parameter): Deserialize<'de> on a Cow<'a, str> needs care; an into_owned() variant or 'static type is the path of least friction.

Severity P2: serde derives are additive (non-breaking to add later), but the absence right now signals the design hasn't fully committed to non-negotiable #6's cacheable-by-default stance.
title: serde feature derives only on IdentityError; ServerName / MailboxName not serializable
